[prev. author] 3.109, compare 4.56]]; οἱ τοιοῦτοι ὄ. undisciplined masses like these,[ [[prev. work] 126; ὄ. μᾶλλον ἢ στρατός 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 6.7.1]]; of the camp-followers, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.4.26, 4.3.26, etc.]] — __2 in political sense, populace, mob, opposed to δῆμος (people), [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.8, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 304d; πρὸς ὄχλον ζῶν [prev. author] “Ax.” 368d; οἱ ὁμότιμοι ὤκνουν τὴν τοῦ ὄ. ἰσομοιρίαν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.2.21]]; δικαστηρίων καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ὄ. and popular assemblies (in a contemptuous sense), [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 455a, compare “Euthd.” 290a: proverbial, δι᾽ ὄχλου ἤδη τοῦτό γε]] this is already in the mouths of the people, [ [1st c.BC: Dionysius Halicarnassensis “de Lysia” 10, compare 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Bellum Judaicum” 2.13.1, 4.9.2.]] — __3 generally, mass, multitude, ὄ. τὸν πλεῖστον λόγων [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 827; τὸν πλεῖστον ὄ. τῶν πραχθέντων 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 12.192]]; ἵππων ὄ. [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 191 (Lyric poetry); ἄκριτος ἄστρων ὄ. 5th c.BC: Critias Philosophus, Tragicus, Elegiacus 19.5 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator; σαρκῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Timaeus” 75e]]: in plural, the masses, καχεξία τις ὑποδέδυκε τοὺς ὄχλους [ [4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 24.4, compare 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 161.1, 466.4; πιθανώτεροι οἱ ἀπαίδευτοι ἐν τοῖς ὄ. 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rhetorica” 1395b28.]] — __II annoyance, trouble, σχολὴν ὄ. τε μέτριον [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Ion” 635, etc.]]; ὄχλον παρέχειν to give trouble, [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 337, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 3.2.27, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 84d]]; δι᾽ ὄχλου εἶναι, γενέσθαι, to be or become troublesome, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 888, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.73, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus Alcaeus1.103a; μάταιον ὄ. τοὺς λόγους νομίσητε 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18.214; οἱ δὲ ἀντιλέγοντες ὄ. ἄλλως καὶ βασκανία κατεφαίνετο [prev. author] 19.24.]]
G3794: ὀχῠρ-ωμα, ατος, τό, — stronghold, fortress, prison, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 3.2.3, LXX.Gen.39.20, “PPetr.” 2p.34 (3rd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.6.3, “PStrassb.” 85.23 (2nd c.BC): _plural_, 1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus “Rh.” 1.334 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus, “OGI” 455.14 (Aphrodisias, 1st c.BC).]]
G3795: ὀψ-άριον, τό, — diminutive of ὄψον, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Fragmenta” 45, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 95, 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 27, 4th-3rd c.BC: Philemo Comicus 32, “Test.Epict.” 6.11, “PPetr.” 3p.327 (3rd c.BC), “PCair.Zen.” 440.3 (3rd c.BC), etc.]]; λαγύνιον ταριχηροῦ (i.e. -ῶν) ὀψαρίων a jar of pickled fish, [ [“BGU” 1095.17 (1st c.AD),compare “PRyl.” 229.21 (1st c.AD), NT.John.6.9, +others, “OGI” 484.12 (Pergam., 2nd c.AD).]]
G3796: ὀψέ, — Aeolic dialect ὄψι (which see), adverb after a long time, at length, late, ἔκ τε καὶ ὀ. τελεῖ, opposed to αὐτίκα, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 4.161; ὀ. κακῶς ἔλθοι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.534, etc.]]; ὀ. διδάσκεσθαι, μανθάνειν, to be late in learning, learn too late, [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1425, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 1264; ὀψέ γε φρονεῖς εὖ 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 99; also ὀ. δή 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.399, etc.; ὀ. γοῦν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus [same place]; ὀ. περ 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 3.80.]] — __b ὀ. ἀφ᾽ οὗ.. it is not long since.., [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.14.]] — __2 late in the day, at even, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.232, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.272, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.106, etc.]]; ὀφλεῖν.. ὀ. ὁδοῦ incur a penalty for being out late at night, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 433a (uncertain)]]; late in the season, [ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 485]]; ὀ. ἦν, ὀ. ἐγίγνετο, it was, it was getting, late, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 2.2.16, 3.4.36]]; ἡ μάχη ἐτελεύτα ἐς (variant{ἕως}) ὀ. did not end till late, [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.108; so ἐς ὀψέ [prev. author] 8.23]]; but εἰς ὀ. ψηφίζεσθαι continue voting till late in the day, [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.15.]] — __3 with genitive, ὀ. τῆς ἡμέρας late in the day, ἤδη γὰρ τῆς ἡμέρας ὀ. ἦν [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.93, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 2.1.23; so perhaps ὀ. σαββάτων after the sabbath day, [ [NT.Matt.28.1.—For the _comparative_ and _superlative_ _adverbs_ see at {ὄψιος}.]]
G3797: ὄψῐμος, ον, — (ὀψέ) poetry for ὄψιος, late, slow, τέρας ὄ. for (concerned with) a late time, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.325]]: in Prose, late in the season, σπόρος [ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Oeconomicus” 17.4, 5, but _falsa lectio_ for{ὄψιος} in 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “Historia Plantarum” 1.9.7, +others]]; of crops, [ [LXX.Exo.9.32, “PSI” 4.433.2 (3rd c.BC), “PCair.Zen.” 299.2 (3rd c.BC)]]; ἐν τοῖς ὀ. τῶν ὑδάτων [ [1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.10; ὑετὸς πρώϊμος καὶ ὄ. NT.Jam.5.7]]: comparative, καιρὸς -ώτερος [ [“PFay.” 133.9 (3rd c.AD)]]; recent, ποιητική [ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.674f]]. adverb -μως[ [“PTeb.” 72.361 (2nd c.BC), “POxy.” 474.24 (2nd c.AD), 5th c.AD: Proclus Philosophus ad 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 483.]]
G3798: ὀψία, — Ionic dialect -ιη (i.e. ὥρα), ἡ, the latter part of day, evening, opposed to ὄρθρος, frequently joined with δείλη (which see), μέχρι δείλης ὀψίης [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.167; περὶ δείλην ὀ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.26]]; δείλης ὀ. late in the evening, [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.9]]; ὀψίας alone, [ [“POxy.” 528.5 (2nd c.AD).]] —Cf. ὄψιος.
G3799: ὄψις, ἡ, — genitive εως, Ionic dialect ιος, (ὄπωπα): — __I objective, aspect, appearance of a person or thing, πατρὸς φίλου ὄψιν ἀτυχθείς [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.468; εἰσορόων ὄ. τ᾽ ἀγαθὴν καὶ μῦθον ἀκούων 24.632, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1412 (_anapaest meter_); δῶρον, οὐ σπουδαῖον εἰς ὄ. [prev. author] “OC” 577]]; πλείω τὴν ὄ. παρείχετο made the appearance greater, [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.46; ἀξιόλογον ὄ. παρέχεται τὸ δένδρος “PCair.Zen.” 157.4 (3rd c.BC)]]; ὥστε ὄ. καλὴν φαίνεσθαι [ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 5.9.9; εἰκάζεσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς φανερᾶς ὄ. 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.10; τὴν ὄ. τοῦ σώματος προορᾶν [prev. author] 7.44]]: the accusative is used absolutely, in appearance, τῷ ὄψιν ἐειδόμενος [ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 10.15; στρογγύλος τὴν ὄ. 5th c.BC: Hermippus Comicus 4; ἀστειότατον τὴν ὄ. 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 59]]; καλός τε κἀγαθὸς τὴν ὄ. [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Parmenides” 127b]]; ἀπὸ τῆς ὄ. Ἑλληνικός to judge from his looks, [ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 33.2; so ἐκ τῆς ὄ. “POxy.” 37 ii 3 (1st c.AD).]] — __I.b countenance, face, [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 905, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 240d, 254b, etc.]]; διοίδησις ὅλης ὄ. [ [1st c.AD: Herodotus Medicus in “Rh.Mus.” 58.83, compare 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.44, 3rd c.AD: Philumenus Medicus cited in 6th c.AD: Aëtius Medicus 9.7]]; οὐκ ἄξιον ἀπ᾽ ὄψεως οὔτε φιλεῖν οὔτε μισεῖν οὐδένα by the face or look merely, [ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 16.19]]; ἀδήλως τῇ ὄ. πλασάμενος so that nothing could be learnt from his countenance, [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 6.58; τίνι δεδούλωταί ποτ; ὄψει 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 541.2: _plural_, 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 98.6, 4th c.BC: Anaxandrides Comicus 41.38.]] — __I.c visual impression or image of an object, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 193c.]] — __I.2 thing seen, sight, φοβερὰν ὄ. προσιδέσθαι [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 48 (_anapaest meter_), compare “Supp.” 567 (Lyric poetry); ὁρῶ Πυλάδην.., ἡδεῖαν ὄ. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 727, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 887d, etc.]]; ἄλλην ὄ. οἰκοδομημάτων other architectural sights, [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.136]]; τὰ δὲ χρήματα.. ἔστιν ὄψις mere outside show, [ [4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 33.2; πολλὴν ὄ. παρασχόντα ἔπειτα μηδὲν ὠφελῆσαι 5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “περὶ ἄρθρων ἐμβολῆς” 44]]; of scenic representations, [ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1453b1, +others; ὁ τῆς ὄ. κόσμος [prev. work] 1449b33: _plural_, [prev. work] 1462a16.]] — __I.3 vision, apparition, [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.39, etc.; ὄ. ἐν τῷ ὕπνῳ [prev. author] 3.30, +others; ὄ. ἐνυπνίου [prev. author] 8.54; ὄ. ὀνείρου [prev. author] 1.38; ὄ. ἔννυχοι 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 645, compare “Ag.” 425 (Lyric poetry), 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 413, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hecuba” 72 (Lyric poetry), “IG” 42(1).121.11 (Epid., 4th c.BC), etc.]] — __II subjective, power of sight or seeing, vision, ὄψει τινὰ ἰδεῖν, ἐσιδεῖν, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 20.205, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 25.94, compare 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 55, 3rd c.AD: Democritus Epigrammaticus 11, 5th c.BC: Empedocles Poeta Philosophus 4.10, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.75, etc.]]; τῆς ἐμῆς ὄ. [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.99, 147; τῆς ὄ. στερηθῆναι [prev. author] 9.93, etc.]]; οὐ τὸ δρασθὲν πιστότερον ὄψει λαβόντες ἢ τὸ ἀκουσθέν [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.38; οὐ καθορωμένους τῇ ὄ. νυκτὸς οὔσης [prev. work] 112.]] — __II.b act of seeing or looking, ἡ εἰς τὸ ἄνω ὄ. [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 396b]]; sense of sight, [ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Anima” 428a6, “Mete.” 369b9]]; τὰ διὰ τῆς ὄ., of pleasures, [ [[prev. author] “EN” 1118a3, etc.]] — __II.c plural, organs of sight, eyes, ὄψεις μαρᾶναι to quench the orbs of sight, [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1328, compare “Ant.” 52, 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 26; τὸ κάλλος πάντων εἷλκε τὰς ὄ. ἐπ᾽ αὐτόν 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 1.9]]; ἀσθενῖ (={-εῖ}) τὰς ὄ. [ [“POxy.” 911.6 (3rd c.AD): so in _sing._, ἐστερήθη τῆς μιᾶς ὄ. 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.79.12]]: singular in collective sense, the eyes, [ἰχθῦς] λευκὴν ἔχοντες τὴν ὄ. [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.106]]; ἀποφαίνειν τί τινι ἐς ὄ. [ [[prev. author] 4.81; λυπηρὰς τῇ ὄ. ἀχθηδόνας προστιθέμενοι 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.37; ἐν ὄ. τοῦ δήμου 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Tiberius Gracchus” 12]]; κατ᾽ ὄψιν in person, ὡς ἐνετειλάμην σοι κατ᾽ ὄ. as I enjoined you when with you, [ [POxy. 1154.4 (1st c.AD), compare 117.3 (2nd-3rd c.AD), etc.]] — __II.2.b dignity, position, κατὰ τὴν ἐμὴν ὄ. καὶ ὑπόλημψιν [ [“PLond.” 1.77.59 (6th c.AD)]]; ἡ τῶν γονέων ἡμῶν προτεραία ὄ. [ [“PMasp.” 2 iii6 (6th c.AD).]]
G3800: ὀψώνιον, τό, — (ὄψον, ὠνέομαι) salary, reckoned in money, τό τε ὀ. καὶ σιτομετρίαν καὶ τὸ ἔλαιον [ [“PCair.Zen.” 507.5, compare 421.6, 483.14, 498.5 (all 3rd c.BC); ἵνα ἡμῖν ὀ. προστεθῇ καὶ σιτάριον [prev. work] 49.4 (3rd c.BC)]]; μετρήματα καὶ ὀ. corn- and money-payments, [ [“UPZ” 14.26 (2nd c.BC)]]; φυλακιτῶν [ [“PPetr.” 3p.230 (3rd c.BC)]]; of a bank clerk, [ [“PCair.Zen.” 342.6 (3rd c.BC): distinguished from γραμματικόν (bonus on turnover), “PStrassb.” 105.4 (3rd c.BC)]]; χωρὶς ὀψωνίων, of unsalaried services, [ [“Inscription Prien.” 121.34 (1st c.BC).]] — __2 a policeman's pay, [ [PLille 25.55 (3rd c.BC), “PFay.” 302 (2nd c.BC), “IG” 9(2).1109.27 (Thess., 2nd-1st c.BC)]]; frequently a soldier's pay, [ [PStrassb. 103.16 (3rd c.BC), “PTheb.Bank” 6.7 (2nd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 6.39.12]]: so in plural, pay of an army, [ [“Rev.Ét.Anc.” 33.8 (Theangela, 4th-3rd c.BC), “OGI” 229.106 (3rd c.BC), “SIG” 410.19 (3rd c.BC), 581.34 (2nd-1st c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.67.1, 3.25.4, LXX.1Mac.3.28, Aristeas 22.]] — __3 allowance paid to a victorious athlete, [ [“PRyl.” 153.25 (2nd c.AD), “CPHerm.” 54.7, +others (3rd c.AD)]]; allowance or scholarship paid to a music-student, προδοῦναί μοι τὸ ὀ. καὶ τὸ κατὰ μῆνα ἀνάλωμα [ [“PCair.Zen.” 440.6 (3rd c.BC)]]; allowance to a son or daughter, [ [“BGU” 665 ii 15 (1st c.AD), “POxy.” 898.31 (2nd c.AD)]]; to a slave, distinguished from ἱματις μός, [ [“PCair.Zen.” 28.6, 100.14 (3rd c.BC).]] — __4 wages of labour, τὰ σώματα ἐνοχλεῖ ἡμᾶς τὰ ὀ. ἀπαιτοῦντα [ [[prev. work] 43.2, compare 27.2, +others, “PPetr.” 2p.113 (all 3rd c.BC), “POxy.” 974 (3rd c.AD)]]; ἀρτάβην κριθῆς εἰς λόγον ὀψωνίων [ [“PTeb.” 420.24 (3rd c.AD): _metaphorically_, ὀψώνια ἁμαρτίας]] the wages of sin, [ [NT.Rom.6.23.]] — __5 a magician's fee, [ [PMag.Par. 1.2454.]] — __6 gratuity to tax-farmers, [ [“UPZ” 112v3 (_plural_).]] — __7 ={ὄψον} [ [I.1 (cf. Latin]]obsonium), τῶν ἀνηλωμάτων πάντων σίτου καὶ ὀψωνίων [ [[prev. work] 91.13 (2nd c.BC).]]—The word is rejected by [ [2nd c.AD: Phrynichus Atticista 393. First used by 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 1051 (no context); ᾔτησεν εἰς ὀ. τριώβολον Thugenides Comicus 2. Glossed ὀψωνία, also (in _plural_) κέρδη, χαρίσματα, by 9th c.AD: Photius Legal icographus, etc.]]

πῶς· πός, ὑπὸ Δωριέων, [ [5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus]] (perhaps πός· πούς, ὑ.Δ.); Laconian dialect πόρ, [ [[prev. author] (on the accent see Hdn.Gr. 2.921, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Adverbiis;” 134.24)]]:—foot, both of men and beasts, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.212, 8.339 (both _plural_), etc.]]; in plural, also, a bird's talons, [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.526]]; arms or feelers of a polypus, [ [8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 524]]: properly the foot from the ankle down wards, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 17.386; ταρσὸς ποδός 11.377, 388]]; ξύλινος π., of an artificial foot, [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.37]]: but also of the leg with the foot, as χείρ for the arm and hand, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 23.772, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 4.149, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 59.]] — __2 foot as that with which one runs, πόδας ὠκὺς Ἀχιλλεύς [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.215, +others; or walks, τῷ δ᾽ ὑπὸ ποσσὶ μέγας πελεμίζετ᾽ Ὄλυμπος 8.443]]; frequently with reference to swiftness, περιγιγνόμεθ᾽ ἄλλων πύξ τε.. ἠδὲ πόδεσσιν [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 8.103]]; ποσὶν ἐρίζειν to race on foot, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.325, compare 23.792; πόδεσσι πάντας ἐνίκα 20.410, compare 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 13.261; ἀέθλια ποσσὶν ἄροντο 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 9.124, etc.]]; ποδῶν τιμά, αἴγλα, ἀρετά, ὁρμά, [ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 12.15, 13.36, “P.” 10.23, 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 9.20; ἅμιλλαν ἐπόνει ποδοῖν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 213 (Lyric poetry): the _dative_ ποσί]] (ποσσί, πόδεσσι) is added to many Verbs denoting motion, π. βήσετο, παρέδραμον, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.389, 23.636; π. θέειν, πηδᾶν, σκαίρειν, πλίσσεσθαι, [prev. work] 622, 21.269, 18.572, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.318; ὀρχεῖσθαι 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Theogonia” 3; ἔρχεσθαι 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 6.39; πάρος ποσὶν οὖδας ἱκέσθαι 8.376; νέρθε δὲ ποσσὶν ἤϊε μακρὰ βιβάς 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 7.212]]; also emphatically with Verbs denoting to trample or tread upon, πόσσι καταστείβοισι [ [7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica 94; [ [5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “P.” 4.132; μουσική 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 668b; τιμαί [prev. author] “R.” 519d; σπέρματα 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 4.4.23]]; δῶρον οὐ σ. εἰς ὄψιν not goodly to look on, [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 577]]; τραγῳδία σ. [ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Poetica” 1449b17; σ. ὑπόδημα [prev. author] “EE” 1219a22]]:— a play on senses [ [11.1 and 11.2 in 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1176b25, 1177a3]]; ironically, σ. χρῆμα a fine thing, [ [“hymnus ad Mercurium” 332.]] — __III adverb σπουδαίως with haste or zeal, seriously, earnestly, well, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.3.9, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Cratylus” 406b, etc.]]: comparative -ότερον[ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 2.3.20]]; -οτέρως [ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Nob.” 15: _superlative_ τὰ -ότατα]] most carefully, in the best way, [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.86.—Besides the regular _comparative_ and _superlative_, we find in _Ionic dialect_ the forms -έστερος, -έστατος, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8, 133, 4th-5th c.BC: Hecataeus Milesius Historicus cited in 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 1441.15, 4th c.AD: Eusebius Myndius Philosophus 4.]]

IV; σὺν σπουδῇ ταχύς [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1223]]; σὺν πάσῃ σ. with all dispatch, [ [POxy. 63.5 (2nd-3rd c.AD)]]; διὰ σπουδῆς [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 212, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Historia Graeca (Hellenica)” 6.2.28, etc.; ἐκ σπουδῆς 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Mirabilia” 837a15]]; μετὰ σ. [ [NT.Mark.6.25, compare 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 6.4.3, etc.; κατὰ σπουδήν 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.93, 2.90, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.6.28, etc. (but this sense frequently runs into the next).]] — __II zeal, pains, trouble, effort, ἄτερ σπουδῆς [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 21.409]]; σῆς ὑπὸ σ. [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 585; σπουδῆς οὐκ ἀξία 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 778, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 604c, etc.]]; frequently in dative σπουδῇ, zealously, see below[ [IV. 3; so σὺν σπουδῇ [prev. author] “Lg.” 818c]]; σὺν πολλῇ σ. [ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.8.4]]; ἐπὶ μεγάλης σ. [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 192c]]; μετὰ πολλῆς σ. [ [[prev. author] “Chrm.” 175e]]; σπουδὴν ποιεῖσθαι exert oneself, take pains, be eager, [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.30]]; with infinitive, [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.4, 7.205; σ. πολλὴν ποιέεσθαι [prev. author] 6.107; πᾶσαν σ. ποιήσασθαι ὅπως.. “PHib.” 1.71.9 (3rd c.BC)]]; σ. ποιεῖσθαι περί τινος [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 177c]]; περί τινα[ [[prev. work] 179d; ἐπί τινι 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Salt.” 1: with _genitive_, σπουδήν τινος ποιήσασθαι]] make much ado about.. , [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.4]]; G5023: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, — genitive τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, etc.: the dual feminine never in Attic dialect, see ὁ, ἡ, τό, [near the start]:—demonstrative pronoun, this, common from [ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards]] — __A ORIGIN and FORMS: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο probably arose from a reduplication of the demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό with insertion of -υ- (= Sanskrit Particle u), e.g. ταῦτα from τα-υ-τα: Doric dialect genitive singular feminine τούτας [ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11; _nominative_ _plural_ τοῦτοι, ταῦται 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 111.23: the former occurs 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 24, “GDI” 3045 B 6 (from Selinus), “SIG” 339.16 (Rhodes, 3rd c.BC)]], etc., the latter is uncertain in [ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 97, certain in “SIG” 241 B 117 (Delph., 4th c.BC): in _Boeotian dialect_ all forms begin with οὑτ-]], as genitive singular neuter οὕτω [ [“Supp.epigram” 3.359.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; accusative singular feminine οὕταν [ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.80; _accusative_ _plural_ _neuter_ οὗτα “SIG” 1185.20 (Tanagra, 3rd c.BC), etc.: _genitive_ _plural_ _feminine_ _Attic dialect_ τούτων, Cretan dialect ταυτᾶν “Leg.Gort.” 5.19; _neuter_ ταύτων “Michel” 1334.10 (Elis, 4th c.BC).—In _Ionic dialect_ sometimes written ταότην, ταο̄τα, “SIG” 283.19 (Chios, 4th c.BC), 46.7 (Halic., 5th c.BC), +others]] —In _Attic dialect_ οὗτος was frequently strengthened by the _demonstrative_ -ί, οὑτοσί, αὑτηί, τουτί, _genitive_ τουτουί, _dative_ τουτῳί, _accusative_ τουτονί; plural nominative οὑτοιί, neuter ταυτί, etc., this man here: sometimes a Particle is inserted between the pronoun and -ί, as αὑτηγί for αὑτηί γε, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 784]]; τουτογί for τουτί γε, [ [[prev. author] “V.” 781, “Av.” 894, +others]]; ταυταγί for ταυτί γε, [ [[prev. author] “Eq.” 492, “Pax” 1057, +others]]; τουτοδί for τουτὶ δέ, [ [[prev. author] “Pl.” 227]]; τουτουμενί for τουτουὶ μέν, [ [[prev. author] “Ra.” 965.]] —In codices the ν ἐφελκυστικόν is sometimes added in the forms οὑτοσίν, οὑτωσίν, and οὑτοσίν is said to be Attic dialect by [ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 59.24, 82.11]]. [This ι is always long, and a long vowel or diphthong before it becomes short, as αὑτη?~Xί, τουτω?~Xί, οὑτοῐί, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 201, “Pl.” 44, “Ach.” 40, etc.]]] — __B USAGE in regard to CONCOR[ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator οὗτος]] is frequently used as a pronoun substantive: hence neuter is followed by genitive, κατὰ τοῦτο τῆς ἀκροπόλιος [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ὕβρεως ἐλήλυθεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.37; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ἥκεις μανίας [prev. author] 36.48; ταῦτα τῶν μαθημάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 278b: but quite as frequently as]] adjective, in which case its substantive commonly takes the Article, οὗτος ὁ ἀνήρ or ὁ ἀνὴρ οὗτος.—But the Article is absent, — __B.1 always in Epic dialect Poets (except [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.114), οὗτος ἀνήρ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.471, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.406, etc.]]: sometimes also in Trag., [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 122 (Lyric poetry), 495, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 406, “OC” 471, 1177: once in an Inscription, τοπεῖα: τούτων τὰ ἡμίσεα τοπείων “IG” 22.1622.135 (4th c.BC).]] — __B.2 sometimes when the Noun is so specified that the Article is not needed, ἐς γῆν ταύτην.., ἥντινα νῦν Σκύθαι νέμονται [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.8; ταύτας ἃς οἱ πατέρες παρέδοσαν μελέτας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.85, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 449d, etc.; πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος, ὃν θρηνεῖς ἀεί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 530.]] — __B.3 when οὗτος is used in local sense, here, see below with [ [1.5.]] — __B.4 when the Noun with which οὗτος agrees stands as its Predicate, αὕτη γὰρ ἦν σοι πρόφασις [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1034]]; δικαστοῦ αὕτη ἀρετή [ἐστι] [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 18a: this exception extends to cases in which the Predicate is not so distinctly separated from the Subject, αἰτίαι μὲν αὗται προυγεγένηντο]] these were the grievances which already existed, [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.66]]; ταύτην φήμην παρέδοσαν this was the report which.., [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 16c: frequently with a _superlative_, κίνησις αὕτη μεγίστη δὴ.. ἐγένετο]] this was notably the greatest movement which.., [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.1, compare 3.113: with πρῶτος [prev. author] 1.55, 98, 6.31, NT.Luke.2.2.]] — __B.5 when 3rd pers. is used for 2nd pers. to express contempt, οὗτος ἀνήρ, οὑτοσὶ ἀνήρ, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 467b, 489b, etc.]] — __B.II though οὗτος usually agrees with the Noun that serves as Predicate, it is not rare to find it in the neuter, μανία δὲ καὶ τοῦτ᾽ ἐστί [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 305; τοῦτο γάρ εἰσι.. εὔθυναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.82, etc.]]: and in plural, οὐκ ἔστι ταῦτα ἀρχή [ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.13; ταῦτ᾽ ἐστὶν ὁ προδότης [prev. author] 2.166]]: so with an explanatory clause added, τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ὁ συκοφάντης, αἰτιᾶσθαι μὲν πάντα ἐξελέγξαι δὲ μηδέν [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.34.]] — __B.II.2 so also with a Noun in apposition, τούτοισιν μὲν ταῦτα μέλει, κίθαρις καὶ ἀοιδή [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.159; [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.10, etc.]] — __B.II.4 the neuter is also used of classes of persons, μελιτοπῶλαι καὶ τυροπῶλαι: τοῦτο δ᾽ εἰς ἕν ἐστι συγκεκυφός [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 854, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 711a]]; or of an abstract fact, οὐκ Ἰοφῶν ζ;—τοῦτο γάρ τοι καὶ μόνον ἔτ᾽ ἐστὶ λοιπὸν ἀγαθόν [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 73.]] — __B.III with Prons., — __B.III.1 personal, οὗτος σύ, in local sense, see below — __B.III.2 interrogative, τί τοῦτ᾽ ἔλεξα; what is this that.. ? [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1173 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ant.” 7]]; ποίοισι τούτοι; for ποῖά ἐστι ταῦτα οἷς [ἔχεις ἐλπίδα]; [ [[prev. author] “OC” 388, compare “Ant.” 1049]]; Νέστορ᾽ ἔρειο ὅν τινα τοῦτον ἄγει whom he brings here, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.612.]] — __B.III.3 with οἷος, [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.377, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 61c.]] — __B.III.4 possessive, πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος this father of thine, [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 530, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.30.]] — __B.III.5 demonstrative, οὗτος ἐκεῖνος, τὸν σὺ ζητέεις, where ἐκεῖνος is the Predicate, [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32; [στρατείαν] ἑνδέκατον μῆνα τουτονὶ ποιεῖται for these eleven months, [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.2, compare 3.4; τριακοστὴν ταύτην ἡμέραν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 27; ταύτας τριάκοντα μνᾶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 463b, etc.]] — __C SIGNIFICATION AND SPECIAL IDIOMS: — __C.I this, to designate the nearer, opposed to ἐκεῖνος, that, the more remote, ταῦτα, like τὰ ἐνταῦθα, things round and about us, earthly things, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 75e (variant)]]; compare ὅδε [near the start]: but οὗτος sometimes indicates that which is not really nearest, but most important, δεῖ.. τὸ βέλτιστον ἀεί, μὴ τὸ ῥᾷστον λέγειν: ἐπὶ ἐκεῖνο μὲν γὰρ ἡ φύσις αὐτὴ βαδιεῖται, ἐπὶ τοῦτο δὲ κτλ. [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.72, compare 51.3 and 18.]] — __C.I.2 when, of two things, one precedes and the other follows, ὅδε properly refers to what follows, οὗτος to what precedes, οὐκ ἔστι σοι ταῦτ᾽, ἀλλά σοι τάδ᾽ ἔστι [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 787, compare ὅδε III. 2: frequently, however, where there are not two things, οὗτος]] refers to what follows, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.377, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.306, etc.]]; οὔκουν.. τοῦτο γιγνώσκεις, ὅτι..; [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 379, etc.]] — __C.I.3 οὗτος is used emphatic, generally in contempt, while ἐκεῖνος denotes praise, ὁ πάντ᾽ ἄναλκις οὗτος, i.e. Aegisthus, [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 301; τούτους τοὺς συκοφάντας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 45a; so 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “de Coron.” uses οὗτος of Aeschines, ἐκεῖνος]] of Philip; but οὗτος is used of Philip, [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.15, 4.3.]] — __C.I.3.b of what is familiar, τούτους τοὺς πολυτελεῖς χιτῶνας, of the Persians, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.8; so, in the political speeches of [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, οὗτοι]] are the opposite party, [ [4.1, 8.7]], etc.; but in the forensic speeches, οὗτοι frequently means the judges, the court, [ [21.134, 36.47.]] — __C.I.5 much like an adverb, in local sense (compare ὅδε [near the start]), τίς δ᾽ οὗτος κατὰ νῆας.. ἔρχεα; who art thou here that comest.. ? [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.82]]; frequently in Attic dialect, τίς οὑτοσ; who's this here? VIII.2. — __C.VI repeated, where for the second we should merely say he or it, τοῖσιν τούτου τοῦτον μέλεσιν.. κελαδοῦντες [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1526, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Laches” 200d.]] — __C.VII ταῦτα is used in some special phrases, — __C.VII.1 ταῦτ᾽, ὦ δέσποτα yes Sir (i. e. ἔστι ταῦτα, ταῦτα δράσω, etc.), [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 142, “Pax” 275, compare “Eq.” III; so ταῦτα δή [prev. author] “Ach.” 815; ταῦτά νυν [prev. author] “V.” 1008]]; so also ἦν ταῦτα even so, true, [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 417.]] — __C.VII.2 ταῦτα μὲν δὴ ὑπάρξει so it shall be, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 78a.]] — __C.VII.3 καὶ ταῦτα μὲν δὴ ταῦτα so much for that, frequently in Attic dialect, as [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 220c.]] — __C.VII.4 ταῦτα at end of a formula in epitaphs, etc., probably short for ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχει or ὁ βίος ταῦτά ἐστιν, e.g. οὐδὶς (= -εὶς) ἀθάνατος: ταῦτα [ [“IG” 14.420; Προκόπι ταῦτα [prev. work]1824; χαίρεται (= -τε) ταῦτα [prev. work]1479, etc.: similarly perhaps in a letter, ἂμ μὴ πέμψῃς, οὐ μὴ φάγω, οὐ μὴ πείνω. ταῦτα “POxy.” 119.15 (2nd-3rd c.AD).]] — __C.VIII Adverbial usages: — __C.VIII.1 ταῦταabsolutely, therefore, that is why.., [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.694; ταῦτ᾽ ἄρα 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 90, “Nu.” 319, 335, 394, +others, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 4.55; ταῦτα δή 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 159, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 174a; ταῦτ᾽ οὖν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 550, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 1358, etc.]]; αὐτὰ ταῦτα ἥκω, ἵνα.. [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310e: τοῦτο]] is rare in this sense, τοῦτ᾽ ἀφικόμην, ὅπως.. εὖ πράξαιμί τι [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 1005]]; αὐτὸ γὰρ τοῦτο just because of this, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 204a.]] — __C.VIII.1.b πρὸς ταῦτα so then, therefore, properly used in indignant defiance, [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 992, 1043, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 971, 1115, 1313, “OT” 426, “OC” 455, etc.]] — __C.VIII.2 καὶ ταῦτα, adding a circumstance heightening the force of what has been said, and that, ἄνδρα γενναῖον θανεῖν, καὶ ταῦτα πρὸς γυναικός [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 627]]: but mostly with a participle, ὅς γ᾽ ἐξέλυσας ἄστυ.., καὶ ταῦθ᾽ ὑφ᾽ ἡμῶν οὐδὲν ἐξειδὼς πλέον [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 37, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 704, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 241e, etc.]]; G5025: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, — genitive τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, etc.: the dual feminine never in Attic dialect, see ὁ, ἡ, τό, [near the start]:—demonstrative pronoun, this, common from [ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards]] — __A ORIGIN and FORMS: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο probably arose from a reduplication of the demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό with insertion of -υ- (= Sanskrit Particle u), e.g. ταῦτα from τα-υ-τα: Doric dialect genitive singular feminine τούτας [ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11; _neuter_ ταύτων “Michel” 1334.10 (Elis, 4th c.BC).—In _Ionic dialect_ sometimes written ταότην, ταο̄τα, “SIG” 283.19 (Chios, 4th c.BC), 46.7 (Halic., 5th c.BC), +others]] —In _Attic dialect_ οὗτος was frequently strengthened by the _demonstrative_ -ί, οὑτοσί, αὑτηί, τουτί, _genitive_ τουτουί, _dative_ τουτῳί, _accusative_ τουτονί; plural nominative οὑτοιί, neuter ταυτί, etc., this man here: sometimes a Particle is inserted between the pronoun and -ί, as αὑτηγί for αὑτηί γε, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 784]]; [This ι is always long, and a long vowel or diphthong before it becomes short, as αὑτη?~Xί, τουτω?~Xί, οὑτοῐί, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 201, “Pl.” 44, “Ach.” 40, etc.]]] — __B USAGE in regard to CONCOR[ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator οὗτος]] is frequently used as a pronoun substantive: hence neuter is followed by genitive, κατὰ τοῦτο τῆς ἀκροπόλιος [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84; G5026: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, — genitive τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, etc.: the dual feminine never in Attic dialect, see ὁ, ἡ, τό, [near the start]:—demonstrative pronoun, this, common from [ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards]] — __A ORIGIN and FORMS: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο probably arose from a reduplication of the demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό with insertion of -υ- (= Sanskrit Particle u), e.g. ταῦτα from τα-υ-τα: Doric dialect genitive singular feminine τούτας [ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11; G5037: τε, — enclitic Particle, with two main uses (see. infr. A, B). — __A as a Conjunction, — __A.I τε.. τε, both.. and, joining single words, phrases, clauses, or sentences, the first τε merely pointing forward to the second, ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.544; ἀγαθῶν τε κακῶν τε 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 669; δίψῃ τε λιμῷ τε 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 491, compare 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 34, 35, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 370, 375; τήν τε νῆσον τήν τε ἤπειρον 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.8, compare 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.3.3, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 373b; λυσόμενός τε θύγατρα, φέρων τ᾽ ἀπερείσι᾽ ἄποινα 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.13; παῖδά τε σοὶ ἀγέμεν Φοίβῳ θ᾽ ἱερὴν ἑκατόμβην ῥέξαι [prev. work] 443]]; the elements joined by τε.. τε are usually short in [ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus]], longer in later Gr., e.g. ἐπειδὴ πρόξενοί τέ εἰσιν Ἀθηναίων καὶ εὐεργέται.., ἔν τε τῇ στήλῃ γέγραπται [ [“IG” 12.103.7; ἥ τε γὰρ γῆ.. εὔυδρός ἐστι, ποταμοί τε δι᾽ αὐτῆς ῥέουσι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.47]]; χρὴ.. τούς τε πρεσβυτέρους ὁμοιωθῆναι τοῖς πρὶν ἔργοις, τούς τε νεωτέρους.. μὴ αἰσχῦναι κτλ. [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.92, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 474c, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.25, 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 1.50]]; τά τε γὰρ ληφθέντα πάντ᾽ ἂν σῴζοιτο οἵ τ᾽ ἀδικήσαντες κατ᾽ ἀξίαν λάβοιεν τὰ ἐπιτίμια Aen.[ [Tact. 16.8, compare “Geoponica” 2.49.1, 12.3.2-3; τούτου γὰρ γενομένου.. τά τε ἐχφόρια Χρυσέρμῳ δυνήσομαι ἀποδοῦναι, ἐγώ τε ἔσομαι παρὰ σοῦ φιλανθρωπίας τετευχώς “PEnteux.” 60.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; κλείειν τε τὰ βλέφαρα δεομένων ἐλπιζόντων τε κοιμηθήσεσθαι [ [2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 16.494]], compare 495,501; this use is common at all times in οὔτε.. οὔτε, μήτε.. μήτε, εἴτε.. εἴτε (which see); τε may be used three or more times, ἔν τ᾽ ἄρα οἱ φῦ χειρί, ἔπος τ᾽ ἔφατ᾽ ἔκ τ᾽ ὀνόμαζεν [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 15.530, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.177, 2.58, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 89s q., 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 17.19s q., 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 19.17, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.3.36:]] —ἑνδεκάτη τε δυωδεκάτη τε probably means the eleventh or twelfth, [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.374, 4.588:]] —sometimes τε.. τε couples alternatives, ἀπόρως εἶχε δοῦναί τε μὴ δοῦναί τε [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Aulidensis” 56, compare “Heracl.” 153, “El.” 391]]; hence we find τε.. ἢ.., [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 143c, “Ion” 535d]]; on ἢ (or ἦ).. τε in [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.289 and 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 524 (Lyric poetry) see at {ἦ} I.3.]] — __A.I.2 the first clause may be negative, the second affirmative, as ἐκκλησίαν τε οὐκ ἐποίει.., τήν τε πόλιν ἐφύλασσε [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.22]]; [ [NT.Rom.7.7.]] — __D Position of τε: — __D.1 in signf. A, as an enclitic, it stands second word in the sentence, clause, or phrase, regardless of the meaning: ἐγγύθι τε Πριάμοιο καὶ Ἕκτορος near both Priam and Hector, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 6.317; ἡμέτεραί τ᾽ ἄλοχοι καὶ νήπια τέκνα 2.136, compare 4.505, 7.295; αἰεί τε δὴ νηλὴς οὺ καὶ θράσους πλέως 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 42 codices, compare 291 (_anapaest meter_); ἄνευ τε δόλου καὶ ἀπάτης 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.69; ὑπέρ τε σοῦ καὶ τῆς ἀδελφῆς “PEnteux.” 6.6 (3rd c.BC)]]; τοῖς τε πόνοις καὶ μαθήμασι [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 537a, compare “Ti.” 70b; hence in 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 897 πόλεος must be taken with what precedes (Porson (at [prev. work]))]]: but article + noun, preposition + noun are frequently regarded as forming a unity indivisible by τε, τοῖς κτανοῦσί τε [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 41 (Lyric poetry); πρὸς βίαν τε [prev. author] “Pr.” 210]]; also the order is frequently determined by the meaning, τε being placed immediately after the word (or first word of a phrase or clause) which it joins to what precedes or to what follows, πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.544; ἔξω δόμων τε καὶ πάτρας 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 665]]; the copulative or preparatory τε precedes many other particles, e.g. τε γάρ, τ᾽ ἄρα, τέ τις. — __D.2 τε is enclitic in signfs. B, C also, and stands early in its sentence, clause, or phrase (see. above), but many particles which follow τε in signf. A precede it in signfs. B, C, e.g. in signfs. B, C we have δέ τε, μέν τε, γάρ τε, ἀλλά τε, δ᾽ ἄρα τε, ὅς ῥά τε, οὔτ᾽ ἄρ τε, καὶ γάρ τίς τε, ὅς τίς τε, καί τε. — __E Etymology: signf. A is found also in Sanskrit ca, Latin -que; for signfs. B and c cf. Sanskrit ca in yá[hudot] káś ca 'whosoever (with following verb)', Latin -que in quisque, ubique, plerique, usque, neque, nec (= non in necopinans, etc.), Gothic ni-h 'not' (also 'and not'), Latin namque (= nam).

μισεῖ τις ἐκεῖνον 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.8]]; as vocative, τὸν Πλοῦτον ἔξω τις κάλει call P. out, somebody, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 1196.]] — __A.II.5 τις, τι may be opposed, expressly or by implication, to οὐδείς, οὐδέν, and mean somebody, something, by meiosis for some great one, some great thing, ηὔχεις τις εἶναι you boasted that you were somebody, [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Electra” 939; ἰσθμόν τιν᾽ [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 647.]] — __A.II.7 with adjectives τις combines to express the idea of a substantive used as predicate, ὥς τις θαρσαλέος καὶ ἀναιδής ἐσσι προΐκτης a bold and impudent beggar, [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.449, compare 18.382, 20.140, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.220]]; ὡς ταχεῖά τις.. χάρις διαρρεῖ in what swift fashion (={ταχέως πως}), [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1266, compare “OT” 618, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.198]]; δεινόν τι ποιεύμενος thinking it a terrible thing, [ [[prev. author] 3.155, 5.33.]] — __A.II.8 with numerals and adjectives expressing number, size, or the like, εἷς δέ τις ἀρχὸς ἀνὴρ.. ἔστω some one man, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.144; τοὺς αὐτοέντας.. τιμωρεῖν τινας (variant τινα) [ [[prev. author] “OT” 107.]] — __A.II.10.b in Philosophic writers, τις is added to the Article to show that the Article is used to denote a particular individual who is not specified in the general formula, although he would be in the particular case, ὁ τὶς ἄνθρωπος the individual man (whoever he may be), this or that man, opposed to ἄνθρωπος (man in general), ὁ τὶς ἵππος, ἡ τὶς γραμματική, [ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Categoriae” 1b4, 8]]; (which see) ὁ, ἡ, τό [ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1.5: later ὅ τις (or ὁ τὶς) much like{ὁ δεῖνα}]], δεῦρο ὅ τις θεός, ὄφθητί μοι in a general formula of invocation, [ [“PMag.Par.” 1.236; αἴρω σε, ἥ τις βοτάνη [prev. work]287; εἰς τήν τινα κρείαν (to be read χρείαν) [prev. work]289.]] — __A.II.10.c frequently in opposed clauses, ὁ μέν τις.., ὁ δὲ.. [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Medea” 1141, “Hec.” 624, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 99b, etc.; ὁ μέν τις.., ἄλλος δὲ.. 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Iphigenia Taurica” 1407; ὁ μὲν.., ὁ δέ τις.. 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 1.4.15: _plural_, οἱ μέν τινες.., οἱ δὲ.. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.127, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.91; οἱ μέν τινες.., οἱ δὲ.., οἱ δέ τινες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 3.2.10, etc.; οἱ μὲν.., οἱ δέ τινες.. [prev. work] 6.1.26]], etc.: also combined with other alternative words, ὁ μέν τις.., ὁ δέ τις.., ἕτερος δέ τις.. [ [[prev. author] “Smp.” 2.6]]; ὁ μὲν.., ἕτερος δέ τις.., ὁ δὲ.., etc., [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Plutus” 162f]]: also in neuter, τὸ μέν τι.., τὸ δέ τι.. [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Epistulae” 358a; τὸ μέν τι.., τὸ δὲ.. 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.40]]; in adverbial sense, τὸ μὲν.., τὸ δέ τι.. partly.., partly.. , [ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.73.4]]; κληρονόμους καταλείπω τὴν θυγατέρα μού τινα καὶ τὸν σύντροφον αὐτῆς τινα καί τινα [prev. work] 1034.2 (2nd c.AD)]]; τίς τινι χαίρειν [ [A to B greeting (in a draft letter),[prev. work] (2nd c.AD).]] — __A.II the neuter τι is used, — __A.II.a collectively, ἦν τι καὶ ἐν ταῖς Συρακούσαις there was a party.. , [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.48]]; μηδέν τι λίαν 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Andromache” 1234:]] —also καί τι καὶ.. ὑποψίᾳ in part also from suspicion, [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.107; καί πού τι καί 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “O.” 1.28.]] — __A.II.12 τίς τε frequently in [ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus, ὡς ὅτε τίς τε 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 3.33, 4.141, see τε 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus]] — __A.II.13 ἤ τις ἢ οὐδείς few or none, next to none, [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.140, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Institutio Cyri (Cyropaedia)” 7.5.45, 2nd-3rd c.AD: Dio Cassius Historicus 47.5, 48.4]]; ἢν γαμῇ ποτ᾽ αὐτὸς ἢ [τις] τῶν ξυγγενῶν [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 1128; ἐν τῶν πόλεων “IG” 12.56.14.--Cf. ὅστις, οὔτις, μήτις, ἄλλο τι.]] — __A.III Accentuation and position of τις: — __A.III.1 accentuation: τις is normally enclitic, but in certain uses is orthotone, i.e. theoretically oxytone (τίς, τινά, τινές, τινῶν, etc.,[ [compare 4th-5th c.AD: Choeroboscus Grammaticus “Scholia in Theodosii Canones” 1.373 H.) and barytone when followed by another word (τὶς]] or τις, τινὰ, τινὲς, τινῶν, etc.). According to [ [Scholia 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus p.240 H. its orthotone accent is τίς (not τὶς), τίνα, τίνες, etc. The orthotone form is used in codices:]] — __A.III.1.a at the beginning of a sentence, τίς ἔνδον..; is any one within? [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 654 (τὶς conjecture Hermann)]]; τί φημ; ={λέγω τι}; am I saying anything? [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 865, “OT” 1471]]; <τίς ἦλθ;> ἦλθέ τις has anybody come? [ [“Somebody” has come, Scholia 2nd c.BC: Dionysius Thrax Grammaticus [same place]]]; τὶς κάθηται, τὶς περιπατεῖ, so and so is sitting (walking), [ [2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 8.97]]; τὶς αἰπόλος καλούμενος Κομάτας [ [Scholia 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.78; τίς ποτε οἰκοδεσπότης.. ἐκοπία 5th-4th c.BC: Aesopus Fabularum Scriptor in “Corpus Glossariorum Latinorum” iii ; or after a pause, πῶς γὰρ ἄν, ἔφην ἐγώ, ὦ βέλτιστε, τὶς ἀποκρίναιτο 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 337e]]; τι οὖν (τὶς ἂν εἴποι) ταῦτα λέγει; [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 1.14 (variant); ἔντοσθεν δὲ γυνά, τι θεῶν δαίδαλμα 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.32; οὐ γυμνὸν τὸ φίλαμα, τι δ᾽ ὦ ξένε καὶ πλέον ἑξεῖς 2nd c.BC: Moschus Bucolicus 1.5 (variant for{τὺ}).]] — __A.III.1.b when τις is opposed to to another τις or to some other word, τισὶ μὲν συμφέρει, τισὶ δ᾽ οὐ συμφέρει [ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1284b40, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.92, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 49a, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 9.2; τινὲς μὲν οὖν.., ἡμεῖς δὲ.. 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.1; τὸ τὶ μὲν ψεῦδος ἔχον, τὶ δὲ ἀληθές 2nd c.AD: Sextus Empiricus Philosophus “adversus Mathematicos” 8.127; ἀλλὰ τινὰ μὲν.., τινὰ δὲ.. 1st c.BC: Geminus Astronomicus 14.6; ποτὲ μὲν πρὸς πάντα, ποτὲ δὲ πρὸς τινά 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 1.48: without such opposition, τοῦτ᾽ εἰς ἀνίαν τοὔπος ἔρχεται τινί]] for a certain person, [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 1138]]. Codices are not consistent; in signification[ [11.5a, 10c, 13]] they make it enclitic; in signification [ [11.5b sometimes enclitic, sometimes orthotone (see. above)]]; sometimes enclitic and orthotone in the same sentence, πάντα δὲ τὰ γιγνόμενα ὑπό τέ τινος γίγνεται καὶ ἔκ τινος καὶ τί [ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Metaphysica” 1032a14, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 165c.]] — __A.III.2 position: — __A.III.2.a τις is rarely first word in the sentence, and rarely follows a pause (see. above [ [111.1a, b)]]; it may stand second word, ἔσκε τις ἐνθάδε μάντις ἀνήρ [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.508, compare 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 8.515, 23.331]]; but in general its position is not far before or after the word to which it belongs in sense, ἀλλ᾽ ἄγε δή τινα μάντιν ἐρείομεν [ [1.62; φυλακὴ δέ τις ἔμπεδος ἔστω 8.521.]] — __A.III.2.b in Ionic dialect Prose it sometimes stands between its genitive and the Article of that genitive, τῶν τις Περσέων [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.85; τῶν τις ἱρέων [prev. author] 2.38; τῶν τινες Φοινίκων [prev. author] 8.90; ἐς τῶν τι ἄλλο στομάτων τοῦ Νείλου [prev. author] 2.179]]; so also in late Prose, [ [2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 3.108d, 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis 1402.18, 1659.27, 1676.1.]] — __A.III.2.c it stands between the Article and substantive in signification[ [11.10b.]] — __A.III.2.d τίς τι is the correct order, not τί τις, “IG” 12.110.46, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 7.10, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.1.14 (codices dett.), 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22.22, etc. — __A.III.2.e whereas in _Attic dialect_ the order ἐάν τις is compulsory, in _Doric dialect_ the usual order is αἴ τίς κα, [ [“Leg.Gort.” 9.43, +others, “Tab.Heracl.” 1.105, +others (but αἴ κά τις 5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 35, 159; αἰ δέ κα μή τις “Leg.Gort.” 5.13)]]: later Doric dialect εἴ τί κα [ [“GDI” 2101.3, +others]]; καἴ τι ἂν (={καὶ εἴ τι ἂν}) [ [“IG” 5(1).1390.50 (Andania, 1st c.BC]], see below [ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 11.1b)]]:—this Doric dialect order influenced the Koine, as in the rare εἴ τις ἂν [ [1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Tiberius Gracchus” 15.]]

see at {ποῖος} I.3 and IV:]] — __B.I in direct questions, who? which? neuter what? which? ὦ ξεῖνοι, τίνες ἐστ; [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 9.252; τί νύ μοι μήκιστα γένητα; 5.299; τίς δαίμων τόδε πῆμα προσήγαγ; 17.446]]; τίς ἀχώ, τίς ὀδμὰ προσέπτα μ᾽ ἀφεγγή; [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 115 (Lyric poetry), compare 561 (_anapaest meter_), etc.]]; properly at the beginning of the sentence; but this position may be varied, — __B.I.a for grammatical reasons, as between the Article and participle or noun, τοὺς τί ποιοῦντας τὸ ὄνομα τοῦτο ἀποκαλοῦσι; [ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Memorabilia” 2.2.1, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 206b]]; τῆς περὶ τί πειθοῦς ἡ ῥητορική ἐστιν τέχν; [ [[prev. author] “Grg.” 454a]]; ὁ σοφιστὴς τῶν τί σοφῶν ἐστι; [ [[prev. author] “Prt.” 312d.]] — __B.I.b for emphasis, ἃ δ᾽ ἐννέπεις, κλύουσα τοῦ λέγει; [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 412, compare “El.” 1191]]; πόλις τε ἀφισταμένη τίς πω.. τούτῳ ἐπεχείρησ; [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.45]]; especially when the Verb begins the sentence, δράσεις δὲ δὴ τ; [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Hercules Furens” 1246]]; κἀνήρετ᾽ ἐν τῷ πράγματος κυροῖ ποτε [prev. author] “Aj.” 314, etc.]] — __B.I.2 sometimes as the predicate, τίς ὀνομάζετα; what is he named? [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 123]]; so also may be explained the union of τίς with a demonstrative or possessive pronoun, or with a Noun preceded by the Article, τί τοῦτ᾽ ἔλεξα; [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1173 (Lyric poetry)]]; τί ἐστι τουτ; τίς ὁ τρόπος τοῦ τάγματο; [ [[prev. author] “Ichn.” 114]]; also with pronoun in plural, τί ταῦτ; [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Phoenissae” 382, “Andr.” 548, etc.]]; τί γὰρ τάδ᾽ ἐστί; [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 200]]; τί ποτ᾽ ἐστίν, ἂ διανοούμεθ; [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 154e]]; τί ποτ᾽ ἐστὶ ταῦτα[ [; [prev. work] 155c; σκεπτέον τί τὰ συμβαίνοντα [prev. author] “Grg.” 508b]]; so τί is used as predicate of a masculine or feminine subject, τί νιν προσείπ; [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Choephori” 983(997)]]; τί σοι φαίνεται ὁ νεανίσκο; [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 154d:]] —also τίς δ᾽ ὅδε Ναυσικάᾳ ἕπεται; who is this that follows N.? τί γά; [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 336 (Lyric poetry)]]:—on ὅτι τ; ὅτι τί δ; ὅτι δὴ τ; see at {ὅτι} [ [5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus 1b]]; on ὡς τ; see {ὡς} F.1. — __B.I.8.b τί τοῦτ; τί ταῦτ; see above 2. — __B.I.8.c τί μο; τί σο; what is it to me? to thee? [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 753, etc.]]; with genitive, τί μοι ἔριδος καὶ ἀρωγῆ; what have I to do with.. ? [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 21.360]]; τί δέ σοι ταῦτ; [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Lysistrata” 514, compare “Ec.” 521]] (where the answerer repeats the question in indirect form, ὅ τί μοι τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι;); ἀλλὰ δὴ τί τοῦτ᾽ ἐμο; [ [4th-3rd c.BC: Diphilus Comicus 32.18]]; τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σο; what have I to do with thee? [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.362, etc.]]; so too in Attic dialect, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 43c, etc.]]; δόμων γὰρ ζῶσι τῶνδε δεσπόται. Answ. τί ζῶσι; how do you mean ζῶσι ζῶσι forsooth! [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Alcestis” 806]]; Κιθαιρὼν--Answ. τί Κιθαιρώ; what aboutK.? [ [[prev. author] “Ba.” 1177 codices, compare 1182 (both Lyric poetry)]]; compare τίη. — __B.I.8.f τί with Particles: -τί γά; why not? how else? and so it came to mean of course, no doubt, [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 1239, “Ch.” 880, “Eu.” 678, etc.]]; used in affirmative answers, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedrus” 258d, “Tht.” 209b, +others]]; to introduce an argument, [ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Politica” 1281a14; see at {γάρ} I.4:]] —τί δαί; see at {δαί}:—τί δ; serving to pass on quickly to a fresh point, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Hp.Ma.” 288c, +others]]; τί δέ, εἰ..; but what, if.. ? [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Helena” 1043]]; τί δ᾽ ἄν, εἰ..; [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Thesmophoriazusae” 773]]; τί δ᾽ ἢν..; [ [[prev. author] “Nu.” 1444]]; τί δέ, εἰ μὴ..; what else but.. ? G5123: τουτέστι, — ={τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι}, that is to say, [ [NT.Mark.7.2, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.64c, 7th c.AD: Hephaestio Grammaticus 12.1, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 29.13, “Codex Justinianus [4th-6th c.AD]” 1.1.5.3, etc.]]; falsa lectio in [ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 94 (codices SM 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes).]]
G5124: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, — genitive τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, etc.: the dual feminine never in Attic dialect, see ὁ, ἡ, τό, [near the start]:—demonstrative pronoun, this, common from [ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards]] — __A ORIGIN and FORMS: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο probably arose from a reduplication of the demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό with insertion of -υ- (= Sanskrit Particle u), e.g. ταῦτα from τα-υ-τα: Doric dialect genitive singular feminine τούτας [ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11; _nominative_ _plural_ τοῦτοι, ταῦται 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 111.23: the former occurs 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 24, “GDI” 3045 B 6 (from Selinus), “SIG” 339.16 (Rhodes, 3rd c.BC)]], etc., the latter is uncertain in [ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 97, certain in “SIG” 241 B 117 (Delph., 4th c.BC): in _Boeotian dialect_ all forms begin with οὑτ-]], as genitive singular neuter οὕτω [ [“Supp.epigram” 3.359.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; accusative singular feminine οὕταν [ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.80; _accusative_ _plural_ _neuter_ οὗτα “SIG” 1185.20 (Tanagra, 3rd c.BC), etc.: _genitive_ _plural_ _feminine_ _Attic dialect_ τούτων, Cretan dialect ταυτᾶν “Leg.Gort.” 5.19; _neuter_ ταύτων “Michel” 1334.10 (Elis, 4th c.BC).—In _Ionic dialect_ sometimes written ταότην, ταο̄τα, “SIG” 283.19 (Chios, 4th c.BC), 46.7 (Halic., 5th c.BC), +others]] —In _Attic dialect_ οὗτος was frequently strengthened by the _demonstrative_ -ί, οὑτοσί, αὑτηί, τουτί, _genitive_ τουτουί, _dative_ τουτῳί, _accusative_ τουτονί; plural nominative οὑτοιί, neuter ταυτί, etc., this man here: sometimes a Particle is inserted between the pronoun and -ί, as αὑτηγί for αὑτηί γε, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 784]]; τουτογί for τουτί γε, [ [[prev. author] “V.” 781, “Av.” 894, +others]]; ταυταγί for ταυτί γε, [ [[prev. author] “Eq.” 492, “Pax” 1057, +others]]; τουτοδί for τουτὶ δέ, [ [[prev. author] “Pl.” 227]]; τουτουμενί for τουτουὶ μέν, [ [[prev. author] “Ra.” 965.]] —In codices the ν ἐφελκυστικόν is sometimes added in the forms οὑτοσίν, οὑτωσίν, and οὑτοσίν is said to be Attic dialect by [ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 59.24, 82.11]]. [This ι is always long, and a long vowel or diphthong before it becomes short, as αὑτη?~Xί, τουτω?~Xί, οὑτοῐί, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 201, “Pl.” 44, “Ach.” 40, etc.]]] — __B USAGE in regard to CONCOR[ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator οὗτος]] is frequently used as a pronoun substantive: hence neuter is followed by genitive, κατὰ τοῦτο τῆς ἀκροπόλιος [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ὕβρεως ἐλήλυθεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.37; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ἥκεις μανίας [prev. author] 36.48; ταῦτα τῶν μαθημάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 278b: but quite as frequently as]] adjective, in which case its substantive commonly takes the Article, οὗτος ὁ ἀνήρ or ὁ ἀνὴρ οὗτος.—But the Article is absent, — __B.1 always in Epic dialect Poets (except [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.114), οὗτος ἀνήρ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.471, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.406, etc.]]: sometimes also in Trag., [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 122 (Lyric poetry), 495, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 406, “OC” 471, 1177: once in an Inscription, τοπεῖα: τούτων τὰ ἡμίσεα τοπείων “IG” 22.1622.135 (4th c.BC).]] — __B.2 sometimes when the Noun is so specified that the Article is not needed, ἐς γῆν ταύτην.., ἥντινα νῦν Σκύθαι νέμονται [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.8; ταύτας ἃς οἱ πατέρες παρέδοσαν μελέτας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.85, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 449d, etc.; πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος, ὃν θρηνεῖς ἀεί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 530.]] — __B.3 when οὗτος is used in local sense, here, see below with [ [1.5.]] — __B.4 when the Noun with which οὗτος agrees stands as its Predicate, αὕτη γὰρ ἦν σοι πρόφασις [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1034]]; δικαστοῦ αὕτη ἀρετή [ἐστι] [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 18a: this exception extends to cases in which the Predicate is not so distinctly separated from the Subject, αἰτίαι μὲν αὗται προυγεγένηντο]] these were the grievances which already existed, [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.66]]; ταύτην φήμην παρέδοσαν this was the report which.., [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 16c: frequently with a _superlative_, κίνησις αὕτη μεγίστη δὴ.. ἐγένετο]] this was notably the greatest movement which.., [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.1, compare 3.113: with πρῶτος [prev. author] 1.55, 98, 6.31, NT.Luke.2.2.]] — __B.5 when 3rd pers. is used for 2nd pers. to express contempt, οὗτος ἀνήρ, οὑτοσὶ ἀνήρ, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 467b, 489b, etc.]] — __B.II though οὗτος usually agrees with the Noun that serves as Predicate, it is not rare to find it in the neuter, μανία δὲ καὶ τοῦτ᾽ ἐστί [ [5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 305; τοῦτο γάρ εἰσι.. εὔθυναι 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 19.82, etc.]]: and in plural, οὐκ ἔστι ταῦτα ἀρχή [ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.13; ταῦτ᾽ ἐστὶν ὁ προδότης [prev. author] 2.166]]: so with an explanatory clause added, τοῦτο γάρ ἐστιν ὁ συκοφάντης, αἰτιᾶσθαι μὲν πάντα ἐξελέγξαι δὲ μηδέν [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 57.34.]] — __B.II.2 so also with a Noun in apposition, τούτοισιν μὲν ταῦτα μέλει, κίθαρις καὶ ἀοιδή [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.159; [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.10, etc.]] — __B.II.4 the neuter is also used of classes of persons, μελιτοπῶλαι καὶ τυροπῶλαι: τοῦτο δ᾽ εἰς ἕν ἐστι συγκεκυφός [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Equites” 854, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 711a]]; or of an abstract fact, οὐκ Ἰοφῶν ζ;—τοῦτο γάρ τοι καὶ μόνον ἔτ᾽ ἐστὶ λοιπὸν ἀγαθόν [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 73.]] — __B.III with Prons., — __B.III.1 personal, οὗτος σύ, in local sense, see below — __B.III.2 interrogative, τί τοῦτ᾽ ἔλεξα; what is this that.. ? [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1173 (Lyric poetry), compare “Ant.” 7]]; ποίοισι τούτοι; for ποῖά ἐστι ταῦτα οἷς [ἔχεις ἐλπίδα]; [ [[prev. author] “OC” 388, compare “Ant.” 1049]]; Νέστορ᾽ ἔρειο ὅν τινα τοῦτον ἄγει whom he brings here, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 11.612.]] — __B.III.3 with οἷος, [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.377, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 61c.]] — __B.III.4 possessive, πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος this father of thine, [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 530, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 7.3.30.]] — __B.III.5 demonstrative, οὗτος ἐκεῖνος, τὸν σὺ ζητέεις, where ἐκεῖνος is the Predicate, [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.32; [στρατείαν] ἑνδέκατον μῆνα τουτονὶ ποιεῖται for these eleven months, [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.2, compare 3.4; τριακοστὴν ταύτην ἡμέραν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 27; ταύτας τριάκοντα μνᾶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 463b, etc.]] — __C SIGNIFICATION AND SPECIAL IDIOMS: — __C.I this, to designate the nearer, opposed to ἐκεῖνος, that, the more remote, ταῦτα, like τὰ ἐνταῦθα, things round and about us, earthly things, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 75e (variant)]]; compare ὅδε [near the start]: but οὗτος sometimes indicates that which is not really nearest, but most important, δεῖ.. τὸ βέλτιστον ἀεί, μὴ τὸ ῥᾷστον λέγειν: ἐπὶ ἐκεῖνο μὲν γὰρ ἡ φύσις αὐτὴ βαδιεῖται, ἐπὶ τοῦτο δὲ κτλ. [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.72, compare 51.3 and 18.]] — __C.I.2 when, of two things, one precedes and the other follows, ὅδε properly refers to what follows, οὗτος to what precedes, οὐκ ἔστι σοι ταῦτ᾽, ἀλλά σοι τάδ᾽ ἔστι [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 787, compare ὅδε III. 2: frequently, however, where there are not two things, οὗτος]] refers to what follows, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.377, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.306, etc.]]; οὔκουν.. τοῦτο γιγνώσκεις, ὅτι..; [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 379, etc.]] — __C.I.3 οὗτος is used emphatic, generally in contempt, while ἐκεῖνος denotes praise, ὁ πάντ᾽ ἄναλκις οὗτος, i.e. Aegisthus, [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 301; τούτους τοὺς συκοφάντας 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Crito” 45a; so 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator “de Coron.” uses οὗτος of Aeschines, ἐκεῖνος]] of Philip; but οὗτος is used of Philip, [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 2.15, 4.3.]] — __C.I.3.b of what is familiar, τούτους τοὺς πολυτελεῖς χιτῶνας, of the Persians, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 1.5.8; so, in the political speeches of [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator, οὗτοι]] are the opposite party, [ [4.1, 8.7]], etc.; but in the forensic speeches, οὗτοι frequently means the judges, the court, [ [21.134, 36.47.]] — __C.I.5 much like an adverb, in local sense (compare ὅδε [near the start]), τίς δ᾽ οὗτος κατὰ νῆας.. ἔρχεα; who art thou here that comest.. ? [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 10.82]]; frequently in Attic dialect, τίς οὑτοσ; who's this here? G5125: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, — genitive τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, etc.: the dual feminine never in Attic dialect, see ὁ, ἡ, τό, [near the start]:—demonstrative pronoun, this, common from [ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards]] — __A ORIGIN and FORMS: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο probably arose from a reduplication of the demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό with insertion of -υ- (= Sanskrit Particle u), e.g. ταῦτα from τα-υ-τα: Doric dialect genitive singular feminine τούτας [ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11; _nominative_ _plural_ τοῦτοι, ταῦται 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 111.23: the former occurs 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 24, “GDI” 3045 B 6 (from Selinus), “SIG” 339.16 (Rhodes, 3rd c.BC)]], etc., the latter is uncertain in [ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 97, certain in “SIG” 241 B 117 (Delph., 4th c.BC): in _Boeotian dialect_ all forms begin with οὑτ-]], as genitive singular neuter οὕτω [ [“Supp.epigram” 3.359.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; accusative singular feminine οὕταν [ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.80; _accusative_ _plural_ _neuter_ οὗτα “SIG” 1185.20 (Tanagra, 3rd c.BC), etc.: _genitive_ _plural_ _feminine_ _Attic dialect_ τούτων, Cretan dialect ταυτᾶν “Leg.Gort.” 5.19; _neuter_ ταύτων “Michel” 1334.10 (Elis, 4th c.BC).—In _Ionic dialect_ sometimes written ταότην, ταο̄τα, “SIG” 283.19 (Chios, 4th c.BC), 46.7 (Halic., 5th c.BC), +others]] —In _Attic dialect_ οὗτος was frequently strengthened by the _demonstrative_ -ί, οὑτοσί, αὑτηί, τουτί, _genitive_ τουτουί, _dative_ τουτῳί, _accusative_ τουτονί; plural nominative οὑτοιί, neuter ταυτί, etc., this man here: sometimes a Particle is inserted between the pronoun and -ί, as αὑτηγί for αὑτηί γε, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 784]]; τουτογί for τουτί γε, [ [[prev. author] “V.” 781, “Av.” 894, +others]]; ταυταγί for ταυτί γε, [ [[prev. author] “Eq.” 492, “Pax” 1057, +others]]; τουτοδί for τουτὶ δέ, [ [[prev. author] “Pl.” 227]]; τουτουμενί for τουτουὶ μέν, [ [[prev. author] “Ra.” 965.]] —In codices the ν ἐφελκυστικόν is sometimes added in the forms οὑτοσίν, οὑτωσίν, and οὑτοσίν is said to be Attic dialect by [ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 59.24, 82.11]]. [This ι is always long, and a long vowel or diphthong before it becomes short, as αὑτη?~Xί, τουτω?~Xί, οὑτοῐί, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 201, “Pl.” 44, “Ach.” 40, etc.]]] — __B USAGE in regard to CONCOR[ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator οὗτος]] is frequently used as a pronoun substantive: hence neuter is followed by genitive, κατὰ τοῦτο τῆς ἀκροπόλιος [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ὕβρεως ἐλήλυθεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.37; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ἥκεις μανίας [prev. author] 36.48; ταῦτα τῶν μαθημάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 278b: but quite as frequently as]] adjective, in which case its substantive commonly takes the Article, οὗτος ὁ ἀνήρ or ὁ ἀνὴρ οὗτος.—But the Article is absent, — __B.1 always in Epic dialect Poets (except [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.114), οὗτος ἀνήρ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.471, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.406, etc.]]: sometimes also in Trag., [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 122 (Lyric poetry), 495, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 406, “OC” 471, 1177: once in an Inscription, τοπεῖα: τούτων τὰ ἡμίσεα τοπείων “IG” 22.1622.135 (4th c.BC).]] — __B.2 sometimes when the Noun is so specified that the Article is not needed, ἐς γῆν ταύτην.., ἥντινα νῦν Σκύθαι νέμονται [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.8; ταύτας ἃς οἱ πατέρες παρέδοσαν μελέτας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.85, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 449d, etc.; πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος, ὃν θρηνεῖς ἀεί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 530.]] — __B.3 when οὗτος is used in local sense, here, see below with [ [1.5.]] — __B.4 when the Noun with which οὗτος agrees stands as its Predicate, αὕτη γὰρ ἦν σοι πρόφασις [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1034]]; [στρατείαν] ἑνδέκατον μῆνα τουτονὶ ποιεῖται for these eleven months, [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.2, compare 3.4; τριακοστὴν ταύτην ἡμέραν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 27; ταύτας τριάκοντα μνᾶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 463b, etc.]] — __C SIGNIFICATION AND SPECIAL IDIOMS: — __C.I this, to designate the nearer, opposed to ἐκεῖνος, that, the more remote, ταῦτα, like τὰ ἐνταῦθα, things round and about us, earthly things, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 75e (variant)]]; G5126: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, — genitive τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, etc.: the dual feminine never in Attic dialect, see ὁ, ἡ, τό, [near the start]:—demonstrative pronoun, this, common from [ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards]] — __A ORIGIN and FORMS: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο probably arose from a reduplication of the demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό with insertion of -υ- (= Sanskrit Particle u), e.g. ταῦτα from τα-υ-τα: Doric dialect genitive singular feminine τούτας [ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11; _nominative_ _plural_ τοῦτοι, ταῦται 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 111.23: the former occurs 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 24, “GDI” 3045 B 6 (from Selinus), “SIG” 339.16 (Rhodes, 3rd c.BC)]], etc., the latter is uncertain in [ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 97, certain in “SIG” 241 B 117 (Delph., 4th c.BC): in _Boeotian dialect_ all forms begin with οὑτ-]], as genitive singular neuter οὕτω [ [“Supp.epigram” 3.359.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; accusative singular feminine οὕταν [ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.80; _accusative_ _plural_ _neuter_ οὗτα “SIG” 1185.20 (Tanagra, 3rd c.BC), etc.: _genitive_ _plural_ _feminine_ _Attic dialect_ τούτων, Cretan dialect ταυτᾶν “Leg.Gort.” 5.19; _neuter_ ταύτων “Michel” 1334.10 (Elis, 4th c.BC).—In _Ionic dialect_ sometimes written ταότην, ταο̄τα, “SIG” 283.19 (Chios, 4th c.BC), 46.7 (Halic., 5th c.BC), +others]] —In _Attic dialect_ οὗτος was frequently strengthened by the _demonstrative_ -ί, οὑτοσί, αὑτηί, τουτί, _genitive_ τουτουί, _dative_ τουτῳί, _accusative_ τουτονί; plural nominative οὑτοιί, neuter ταυτί, etc., this man here: sometimes a Particle is inserted between the pronoun and -ί, as αὑτηγί for αὑτηί γε, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 784]]; τουτογί for τουτί γε, [ [[prev. author] “V.” 781, “Av.” 894, +others]]; ταυταγί for ταυτί γε, [ [[prev. author] “Eq.” 492, “Pax” 1057, +others]]; τουτοδί for τουτὶ δέ, [ [[prev. author] “Pl.” 227]]; τουτουμενί for τουτουὶ μέν, [ [[prev. author] “Ra.” 965.]] —In codices the ν ἐφελκυστικόν is sometimes added in the forms οὑτοσίν, οὑτωσίν, and οὑτοσίν is said to be Attic dialect by [ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 59.24, 82.11]]. [This ι is always long, and a long vowel or diphthong before it becomes short, as αὑτη?~Xί, τουτω?~Xί, οὑτοῐί, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 201, “Pl.” 44, “Ach.” 40, etc.]]] — __B USAGE in regard to CONCOR[ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator οὗτος]] is frequently used as a pronoun substantive: hence neuter is followed by genitive, κατὰ τοῦτο τῆς ἀκροπόλιος [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84; G5127: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, — genitive τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, etc.: the dual feminine never in Attic dialect, see ὁ, ἡ, τό, [near the start]:—demonstrative pronoun, this, common from [ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards]] — __A ORIGIN and FORMS: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο probably arose from a reduplication of the demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό with insertion of -υ- (= Sanskrit Particle u), e.g. ταῦτα from τα-υ-τα: Doric dialect genitive singular feminine τούτας [ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11; G5129: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, — genitive τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, etc.: the dual feminine never in Attic dialect, see ὁ, ἡ, τό, [near the start]:—demonstrative pronoun, this, common from [ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards]] — __A ORIGIN and FORMS: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο probably arose from a reduplication of the demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό with insertion of -υ- (= Sanskrit Particle u), e.g. ταῦτα from τα-υ-τα: Doric dialect genitive singular feminine τούτας [ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11; _nominative_ _plural_ τοῦτοι, ταῦται 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 111.23: the former occurs 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 24, “GDI” 3045 B 6 (from Selinus), “SIG” 339.16 (Rhodes, 3rd c.BC)]], etc., the latter is uncertain in [ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 97, certain in “SIG” 241 B 117 (Delph., 4th c.BC): in _Boeotian dialect_ all forms begin with οὑτ-]], as genitive singular neuter οὕτω [ [“Supp.epigram” 3.359.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; accusative singular feminine οὕταν [ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.80; _accusative_ _plural_ _neuter_ οὗτα “SIG” 1185.20 (Tanagra, 3rd c.BC), etc.: _genitive_ _plural_ _feminine_ _Attic dialect_ τούτων, Cretan dialect ταυτᾶν “Leg.Gort.” 5.19; _neuter_ ταύτων “Michel” 1334.10 (Elis, 4th c.BC).—In _Ionic dialect_ sometimes written ταότην, ταο̄τα, “SIG” 283.19 (Chios, 4th c.BC), 46.7 (Halic., 5th c.BC), +others]] —In _Attic dialect_ οὗτος was frequently strengthened by the _demonstrative_ -ί, οὑτοσί, αὑτηί, τουτί, _genitive_ τουτουί, _dative_ τουτῳί, _accusative_ τουτονί; plural nominative οὑτοιί, neuter ταυτί, etc., this man here: sometimes a Particle is inserted between the pronoun and -ί, as αὑτηγί for αὑτηί γε, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 784]]; τουτογί for τουτί γε, [ [[prev. author] “V.” 781, “Av.” 894, +others]]; ταυταγί for ταυτί γε, [ [[prev. author] “Eq.” 492, “Pax” 1057, +others]]; τουτοδί for τουτὶ δέ, [ [[prev. author] “Pl.” 227]]; τουτουμενί for τουτουὶ μέν, [ [[prev. author] “Ra.” 965.]] —In codices the ν ἐφελκυστικόν is sometimes added in the forms οὑτοσίν, οὑτωσίν, and οὑτοσίν is said to be Attic dialect by [ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 59.24, 82.11]]. [This ι is always long, and a long vowel or diphthong before it becomes short, as αὑτη?~Xί, τουτω?~Xί, οὑτοῐί, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 201, “Pl.” 44, “Ach.” 40, etc.]]] — __B USAGE in regard to CONCOR[ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator οὗτος]] is frequently used as a pronoun substantive: hence neuter is followed by genitive, κατὰ τοῦτο τῆς ἀκροπόλιος [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ὕβρεως ἐλήλυθεν 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.37; εἰς τοῦθ᾽ ἥκεις μανίας [prev. author] 36.48; ταῦτα τῶν μαθημάτων 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Euthydemus” 278b: but quite as frequently as]] adjective, in which case its substantive commonly takes the Article, οὗτος ὁ ἀνήρ or ὁ ἀνὴρ οὗτος.—But the Article is absent, — __B.1 always in Epic dialect Poets (except [ [8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 18.114), οὗτος ἀνήρ 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 14.471, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.406, etc.]]: sometimes also in Trag., [ [4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 122 (Lyric poetry), 495, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 406, “OC” 471, 1177: once in an Inscription, τοπεῖα: τούτων τὰ ἡμίσεα τοπείων “IG” 22.1622.135 (4th c.BC).]] — __B.2 sometimes when the Noun is so specified that the Article is not needed, ἐς γῆν ταύτην.., ἥντινα νῦν Σκύθαι νέμονται [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.8; ταύτας ἃς οἱ πατέρες παρέδοσαν μελέτας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.85, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 449d, etc.; πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος, ὃν θρηνεῖς ἀεί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 530.]] — __B.3 when οὗτος is used in local sense, here, see below with [ [1.5.]] — __B.4 when the Noun with which οὗτος agrees stands as its Predicate, αὕτη γὰρ ἦν σοι πρόφασις [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1034]]; δικαστοῦ αὕτη ἀρετή [ἐστι] [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 18a: this exception extends to cases in which the Predicate is not so distinctly separated from the Subject, αἰτίαι μὲν αὗται προυγεγένηντο]] these were the grievances which already existed, [ [5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.66]]; [στρατείαν] ἑνδέκατον μῆνα τουτονὶ ποιεῖται for these eleven months, [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.2, compare 3.4; τριακοστὴν ταύτην ἡμέραν 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus “Ἐπιτρέποντες” 27; ταύτας τριάκοντα μνᾶς 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 27.23, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 463b, etc.]] — __C SIGNIFICATION AND SPECIAL IDIOMS: — __C.I this, to designate the nearer, opposed to ἐκεῖνος, that, the more remote, ταῦτα, like τὰ ἐνταῦθα, things round and about us, earthly things, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 75e (variant)]]; [ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 8.72, compare 51.3 and 18.]] — __C.I.2 when, of two things, one precedes and the other follows, ὅδε properly refers to what follows, οὗτος to what precedes, οὐκ ἔστι σοι ταῦτ᾽, ἀλλά σοι τάδ᾽ ἔστι [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Coloneus” 787, compare ὅδε III. 2: frequently, however, where there are not two things, οὗτος]] refers to what follows, [ [8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.377, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 2.306, etc.]]; G5130: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο, — genitive τούτου, ταύτης, τούτου, etc.: the dual feminine never in Attic dialect, see ὁ, ἡ, τό, [near the start]:—demonstrative pronoun, this, common from [ [8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus downwards]] — __A ORIGIN and FORMS: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο probably arose from a reduplication of the demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό with insertion of -υ- (= Sanskrit Particle u), e.g. ταῦτα from τα-υ-τα: Doric dialect genitive singular feminine τούτας [ [5th-6th c.BC: Philolaus Philosophus 11; _nominative_ _plural_ τοῦτοι, ταῦται 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 111.23: the former occurs 5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 24, “GDI” 3045 B 6 (from Selinus), “SIG” 339.16 (Rhodes, 3rd c.BC)]], etc., the latter is uncertain in [ [5th c.BC: Sophron Comicus 97, certain in “SIG” 241 B 117 (Delph., 4th c.BC): in _Boeotian dialect_ all forms begin with οὑτ-]], as genitive singular neuter οὕτω [ [“Supp.epigram” 3.359.11 (3rd c.BC)]]; accusative singular feminine οὕταν [ [6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica “Supp.” 2.80; _accusative_ _plural_ _neuter_ οὗτα “SIG” 1185.20 (Tanagra, 3rd c.BC), etc.: _genitive_ _plural_ _feminine_ _Attic dialect_ τούτων, Cretan dialect ταυτᾶν “Leg.Gort.” 5.19; _neuter_ ταύτων “Michel” 1334.10 (Elis, 4th c.BC).—In _Ionic dialect_ sometimes written ταότην, ταο̄τα, “SIG” 283.19 (Chios, 4th c.BC), 46.7 (Halic., 5th c.BC), +others]] —In _Attic dialect_ οὗτος was frequently strengthened by the _demonstrative_ -ί, οὑτοσί, αὑτηί, τουτί, _genitive_ τουτουί, _dative_ τουτῳί, _accusative_ τουτονί; plural nominative οὑτοιί, neuter ταυτί, etc., this man here: sometimes a Particle is inserted between the pronoun and -ί, as αὑτηγί for αὑτηί γε, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 784]]; τουτογί for τουτί γε, [ [[prev. author] “V.” 781, “Av.” 894, +others]]; ταυταγί for ταυτί γε, [ [[prev. author] “Eq.” 492, “Pax” 1057, +others]]; τουτοδί for τουτὶ δέ, [ [[prev. author] “Pl.” 227]]; τουτουμενί for τουτουὶ μέν, [ [[prev. author] “Ra.” 965.]] —In codices the ν ἐφελκυστικόν is sometimes added in the forms οὑτοσίν, οὑτωσίν, and οὑτοσίν is said to be Attic dialect by [ [2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 59.24, 82.11]]. [This ι is always long, and a long vowel or diphthong before it becomes short, as αὑτη?~Xί, τουτω?~Xί, οὑτοῐί, [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 201, “Pl.” 44, “Ach.” 40, etc.]]] — __B USAGE in regard to CONCOR[ [4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator οὗτος]] is frequently used as a pronoun substantive: hence neuter is followed by genitive, κατὰ τοῦτο τῆς ἀκροπόλιος [ [5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.84; ταύτας ἃς οἱ πατέρες παρέδοσαν μελέτας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.85, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Respublica” 449d, etc.; πατὴρ σὸς οὗτος, ὃν θρηνεῖς ἀεί 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Electra” 530.]] — __B.3 when οὗτος is used in local sense, here, see below with [ [1.5.]] — __B.4 when the Noun with which οὗτος agrees stands as its Predicate, αὕτη γὰρ ἦν σοι πρόφασις [ [5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Philoctetes” 1034]]; Ἀθηναίων 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.724b]]: frequently with a word to denote the occasion, Λήναια χορηγῶν [ [5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Acharnenses” 1155 (Lyric poetry); χ. παισὶν Διονύσια 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.64; εἰς Ἀπολλώνια “IG” 11(2).106.1 (Delos, 3rd c.BC)]]; ἀνδράσι χ. ἐς Διονύσια [ [5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 21.2; χ. κωμῳδοῖς, πυρριχισταῖς, [prev. work]4; τραγῳδοῖς 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 6.60; κωμῳδοῖς “IG” 22.3090]] (less frequently with the Article added, χ. τὰ Διονύσια τοῖς τραγῳδοῖς [ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 630); also Παναθηναίοις χ. 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 21.156]]:—passive, to have choragi found for one, χορηγοῦσιν μὲν οἱ πλούσιοι, χορηγεῖται δὲ ὁ δῆμος [ [5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Atheniensium” 1.13]]; ἄριστα χορηγοῦνται οἱ παῖδες are well found by their choragus, [ [5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.13.]] — __II.2 metaphorically, minister to, χ. ταῖς σεαυτοῦ ἡδοναῖς [ [4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.240; ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Par.” 12; πρὸς ἐπαινον 4th c.AD: Libanius Sophista “Orationes” 18.7; πρὸς μῆκος λόγου [prev. work] 13.26.]] — __II.3 metaphorically also, — __II.3.a with accusative person, furnish abundantly with a thing, especially with supplies for war, χ. τὸ στρατόπεδον τοῖς ἐπιτηδείοις [ [2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 3.68.8, compare 49.11, 52.7, etc.]]; χρήμασι πρός τι [ [[prev. author] 5.42.7]]:—passive, to be well supplied, τοῖς ἐκτὸς ἀγαθοῖς κεχορηγημένος [ [4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1101a15, compare 1179a11: _absolutely_, κάλλιστα κεχορηγημένος]] best furnished, [ [[prev. author] “Pol.” 1288b14; κεχ. ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον ὥστε.. [ [6th c.BC: Hipponax Iambographus 35.6, compare 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 507 (Lyric poetry), 4th c.BC: Crates Thebanus Poeta Philosophus 10]]; compare χορτάζω. (Cf.
